name: Jinbocho
description: Jinbocho and Kanda from open data, lit by the real sun: the book town's second-hand shops along Yasukuni-dori with their carts of cheap books, the Catholic Kanda Church, and Nikolai-do over Ochanomizu.

seawall.note: The rivers' and the bay's revetments and the castle moats: granite blocks and concrete.

trees.note: Species are not mapped, and the shared trees have no ginkgo or cherry, so the mix stands in: elms for the zelkovas (keyaki), plane trees for the street planes and ginkgos. A guess, not a survey.

tour.title: Jinbocho, from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings. {share:plateau}% of the footprint area stands at a height Project PLATEAU surveyed, on GSI's 5 m laser-scanned bare earth.

tour.title: The book town
tour.text: About 130 second-hand bookshops, most along Yasukuni-dori's south side, facing north to keep the sun off their books; carts of cheap books before every door. The signs here are typical of the street, not its real shops'.

tour.title: Up the hill to Ochanomizu
tour.text: Meiji University's tower, and Nikolai-do's green dome over the Kanda river's gorge.

sources.landmarks: The Catholic Kanda Church (Max Hinder, 1928; registered tangible cultural property; Chiyoda City) on the basilica's footprint of block 1-1, Nishi-Kanda; Nikolai-do as in the Akihabara map. The bookshops' signs are indicative: typical trades, no real shops' signs; the roof names are Sanseido's and Tokyo-do's own words in open fonts.
sources.fonts: Signs drawn with Google Fonts under the SIL Open Font License: Zen Kaku Gothic New, Dela Gothic One, M PLUS Rounded 1c, Bebas Neue, Shippori Mincho

night.note: The bookshops' signs are lit landmark meshes (city.py); the streets' lamps are the country's defaults.

weather.source: Tokyo (Kitanomaru Park): Japan Meteorological Agency, 1991-2020 normals, days with at least 0.5 mm

game.title: Jinbocho on Foot
game.blurb: Walk the book town under the real sun: the second-hand shops and their carts along Yasukuni-dori, a curry for lunch, the Kanda church, and up the hill to Nikolai-do.

npcs.name: Shigeru 茂
idle: My grandfather opened this shop in 1925. The books were the only thing he carried out of the fire in '45.
We face north, all of us, so the sun never fades a spine. {time}.

npcs.name: Kana 佳奈
npcs.role: Curry shop waitress カレー屋
idle: Jinbocho has more curry shops than anywhere in Tokyo. You read with one hand and eat with the other.
Butter, spices and a baked potato on the side. That's the house style. {sun_line}

npcs.name: Takumi 拓海
idle: Every textbook I own came from a cart on Yasukuni-dori. Half the price, and somebody's notes in the margins.
Ochanomizu has the guitar shops. I go to look, not to buy.

npcs.name: Yoko 洋子
idle: The church is from 1928. The first one fell in the earthquake; the Swiss architect who drew this one built half the churches of Tokyo.
Mass is in Japanese, English and Spanish. Everyone sings.

quests.title: Jinbocho
talk: Welcome to Jinbocho. A hundred and thirty bookshops, and I've read most of them.
Look at the carts before you go in. Then go round the back to Suzuran-dori: Kana will feed you.

steps.text: Browse the carts of cheap books

quests.title: Curry and books
talk: Takumi comes in every day with a new old book. He's up at the university now, on the hill.

quests.title: Up the hill
talk: From here, Ochanomizu: the river in its gorge, the trains crossing it, and Nikolai-do's dome.
Go and listen for the bells.

quests.title: The Kanda church
talk: Welcome. Come and look at the front: the rose window lights the nave at sunset.
Inside it's quiet. Even on a weekday, someone is always there.
